summary: First live exercise of myidsan's security keys, with a REAL WebAuthn ceremony (tools/fleetbench/uicheck_idsan_webauthn.js). WebAuthn is the strongest second factor this server offers and the only part of it nothing had ever driven - a FIDO2 ceremony needs a browser and an authenticator, so its unit tests could verify the service and nothing could register a credential, sign in with it, or remove it. Chrome's DevTools WebAuthn domain supplies a virtual CTAP2 authenticator: real key material, real signatures, real client-data hashing, so navigator.credentials runs the genuine ceremony against a genuine attestation and the app's own client code (lib/webauthn.js) is what drives it. The bench found one real defect: the two-factor card on the Profile page announced 'Your account is protected by a password only. Add an authenticator app for a second factor.' whenever TOTP was off, knowing nothing about security keys - so a user who had just enrolled a FIDO2 key was told, on the security page, that they had no second factor. That is a false statement about an account's protection, on the page whose whole job is reporting it, and the kind an operator auditing accounts would act on. The screenshot put the enrolled key and that sentence side by side. WebAuthnKeys now reports its key count to the sibling card, which says something true in either case, in all four languages. Everything else about the surface held up under real use and is now proven rather than assumed: enrolment through the app's own UI; the enrolment recorded in the audit trail (which matters because removing a factor deletes its own evidence); an account whose ONLY factor is a security key still being CHALLENGED at sign-in rather than waved through - the exact MFA-bypass shape the server-rendered login page once had when its challenger was wired for TOTP alone; the key completing that challenge and signing the user in; rename; and removal demanding the password, refusing a wrong one, and being throttled after eight attempts (401 x8 then 429) rather than being the unmetered password oracle it was before PR #206 - now confirmed live from a browser rather than from a test. 19/19 against the fix, 18/19 against unfixed main. Directory/LDAP, the other half of this work item, already has live coverage (infra/login/ldap_integration_test.go against a real OpenLDAP, RUN_LDAP_IT=1) and is unchanged here.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; frontend only, no API, schema or configuration change. The only visible difference is the wording of one banner on the Profile page when an account holds a security key but no authenticator app: it now says the account is protected by a password and a security key, and suggests adding an app so a lost key does not lock the user out, instead of claiming the account has no second factor. Accounts with neither factor see exactly the message they saw before.
